RESEARCH DIRECTION
Build the control systems
around intelligence.

The difficult part is no longer making a model answer. It is making an autonomous system act safely, visibly, recoverably, and usefully.

R/01
Trustworthy agent execution

How can agents act across complex software while remaining observable, recoverable, and constrained?

Reproducible AI claims

What evidence is enough for a model, benchmark, or demo claim to be trusted by a technical reviewer?

Agentic cyber defense

How can specialized agents reduce investigation and response time without hiding critical decisions?

Human-agent coordination

Where should people approve, redirect, or override autonomous workflows to preserve trust and accountability?

Research that remains answerable to reality.
Product-connected

Research questions are tested through working systems, observed failure modes, and real operational constraints.

Transparent about maturity

Security before authority

Accessible under constraint

Useful autonomy should not require unlimited compute, premium hardware, or an expensive API call for every decision.

Start before permission.

Omnia is being built by a Digital Forensics and Cyber Security student in Karachi with a long horizon, limited resources, and an unwillingness to treat those constraints as an excuse.

I am building the lab I want to grow into.

I’m Syed Saad, studying Digital Forensics and Cyber Security at Hamdard University. My strongest interests sit at the intersection of agentic AI, cloud security, infrastructure, digital forensics, and systems that can perform real technical work.

Omnia started as a way to connect projects that would otherwise remain disconnected: crisis intelligence, incident reasoning, network automation, security tooling, and future autonomous workflows.

The operating thesis is simple: every serious build should create reusable code, knowledge, design language, or infrastructure for the next one. Over time, that compounding work can become a platform rather than a collection of demos.

Build something real. Explain what it cannot do. Improve it until the limitation moves.

Lead the plan, absorb the hard last mile, document the work, and make the next execution easier for the team.

Autonomy earns authority
through control.

Least authority

Agents should receive the narrowest tools and permissions required for the current operation.

Observable execution

Recoverable state

Local-first options

Truthful maturity

Experimental capabilities are not described as hardened security controls or production deployments.

I’m Syed Saad, studying Digital Forensics and Cyber Security at Hamdard University. My strongest interests sit at the intersection of agentic AI, cloud security, infrastructure, digital forensics, and systems that can perform real technical work.

Autonomy earns authority

Agents should receive the narrowest tools and permissions required for the current operation.

Observable execution

Material actions should produce traces that a human can inspect, understand, and challenge.

Verification gates

High-impact operations should pause for checks, policy evaluation, or explicit approval.

Recoverable state

Local-first options

Truthful maturity

Experimental capabilities are not described as hardened security controls or production deployments.

Agentic cyber defense

FLAGSHIP PRODUCT / 001
A technical operator for GNS3 labs.

GNS3 Agent is being built to diagnose environments, inspect real GNS3 state, execute bounded workflows, capture evidence, and explain what happened.

Request early access ↗
View GitHub ↗
STATUS
 Active development
CURRENT PHASE
Diagnostics + real REST connectivity
PRIMARY ENVIRONMENT
Windows · GNS3 2.x
OPERATING PRINCIPLE
Read first. Act with boundaries.
01 / PROBLEM
Network labs fail in the gaps
between tools, instructions, and evidence.
01
Environment ambiguity

Python, packages, virtualization, local paths, ports, server processes, and GNS3 versions can fail independently.

02
Execution overhead

Students and engineers repeatedly translate lab documents into device, topology, validation, and troubleshooting steps.

03
Evidence fragmentation

Commands, screenshots, state checks, and written reports are produced separately, often without a reliable audit trail.

02 / CURRENT CAPABILITIES
What the agent can inspect today.

The current phase emphasizes truthful diagnostics and read-only visibility before expanding execution authority.

01
Environment doctor

Python runtime, required packages, Windows paths, GNS3 installation, processes, and virtualization checks.

IMPLEMENTED
02
REST connectivity

Typed direct connection to the GNS3 REST API with structured success and error results.

IMPLEMENTED
03
Server inspection

Server information, projects, templates, configuration, and diagnostic summaries.

IMPLEMENTED
04
Report artifacts

JSON and Markdown reports for diagnostics and read-only inspection output.

IMPLEMENTED
05
Topology execution

Bounded creation and configuration workflows with checkpoints and rollback awareness.

IN PROGRESS
06
Evidence automation

Scope-aware screenshots, command evidence, validation output, and submission-ready reporting.

PLANNED
03 / OPERATING MODEL
A visible execution loop.
01
Understand

Parse the environment, request, lab instructions, constraints, and required evidence.

02
Plan

Produce a device and command plan with validation checkpoints before modifying state.

03
Execute

Call approved tools and GNS3 endpoints through bounded, observable operations.

04
Verify

Check device state, connectivity, expected outputs, and failure conditions.

05
Recover

Stop, explain, retry safely, or return control when confidence or policy is insufficient.

06
Document

Package commands, results, screenshots, and explanations into traceable artifacts.

04 / ARCHITECTURE
Local-first by default. Extensible by design.
01
Interface layer

CLI today; desktop and guided workflow interfaces later.

02
Orchestration layer

Task planning, typed results, policy checks, checkpoints, and execution state.

03
GNS3 adapter

Direct typed REST client for server, project, template, node, and link operations.

04
System diagnostics

Windows process, path, port, package, install, and virtualization inspection.

05
Evidence layer

Structured logs, JSON/Markdown artifacts, screenshots, and report generation.

06
Model layer

Optional reasoning assistance with local or cloud models based on task sensitivity.

05 / INITIAL AUDIENCE
Built first for the people closest to the pain.
Students

Understand lab failures, execute repeatable workflows, and create better evidence without hiding the learning process.

Educators

Standardize lab setup, inspect environments, and reduce time spent debugging unrelated workstation problems.

Technical teams

Automate controlled GNS3 test environments, reusable topology tasks, and infrastructure validation.

EARLY ACCESS
Help shape the first useful release.
